summary: Elevated TTFB on chat completions observed after runtime + model upgrade
slo_sla_details: Customer has enterprise SLA; P1 response required within 2 hours
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-01 07:45 UTC, customer reports significantly elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions. The spike began immediately after a scheduled runtime upgrade and pinned model version update on our us-east-1 serving fleet. Impact: interactive chat flows are timing out or showing 5-10x latency increase to first token, degrading UX and causing higher client-side timeouts. Environment: production, us-east-1, enterprise dedicated account for AcmeAnalytics.
impact: Multiple customers in us-east experienced increased TTFB; AcmeAnalytics reported 30% of chat requests exceeding 5s TTFB and several timeouts. Increased error rates and escalations to CS.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer api key for AcmeAnalytics in prod (us-east-1)
2) Send a chat.completions request with recent prompt (role: user) ~50 tokens expected
3) Measure time-to-first-token via client side headers and server timing
logs: 2026-03-01T07:46:12Z gateway: request-id=abcd1234 received for customer AcmeAnalytics
2026-03-01T07:46:15Z runtime: cold-start tasks queued due to runtime revision r-2026-03-01-1
2026-03-01T07:46:18Z runtime: started first-token generation for request-id=abcd1234 (TTFB measured ~4.2s)
comments: 2026-03-01 08:05 UTC - Support (Ava Chen): Thanks for reporting — investigating with SRE. Can you share a sample request-id and approximate timestamps?
2026-03-01 08:07 UTC - Customer (AcmeAnalytics - Sarah P): Provided request-id=abcd1234 and trace. Observed TTFB spike after your 'r-2026-03-01' runtime update. Chat flows failing in production.

2026-03-01 09:20 UTC - SRE (Diego Martinez): Reproduced locally against prod stack; elevated TTFB correlates with runtime revision r-2026-03-01-1 and model rw-llama-13b-v2. Not seeing increased GPU utilization; suspect kernel selection/quantization path regression.

2026-03-02 02:15 UTC - Eng (Priya Rao): Noted increased cold-start CPU wait due to additional compilation step introduced in r-2026-03-01-1. Preparing a patch to skip redundant compile for pinned models.
2026-03-03 11:45 UTC - Support (Ava Chen): Temporary mitigation applied: rolled back runtime to r-2026-02-28-4 for affected us-east serving pool for AcmeAnalytics. Asking customer to validate UX.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: kernel selection change in runtime revision introduced extra compile/validation step for certain model graphs (rw-llama-13b-v2) leading to cold-first-token delays.
SRE observed that TTFB spike happens even when GPU is idle; blocking occurs on a CPU-side 'compile-and-validate' stage recorded at ~1.9s per request.
Related signals: trace spans show long 'prepare_model' and 'compile_kernels' durations after upgrade, not present before revision r-2026-03-01-1.
Canary checks: staging with same runtime revision shows elevated TTFB only when models are pinned to exact hash; dynamic variant selection did not trigger the compile step.

Potential root causes: conservative safety checks added to kernel selection, changed cache key semantics preventing reuse of compiled artifacts, or a race when multiple requests trigger compile simultaneously.
resolution: Mitigation performed: rolled back runtime r-2026-03-01-1 to r-2026-02-28-4 for affected us-east serving pool for AcmeAnalytics which restored TTFB to baseline (~300ms). Engineering patch in review to skip redundant compilation for pinned models and to fix cache key regression. Follow-ups: deploy patch to canaries, run load tests, then gradually rollout. Customer notified and will monitor for 48 hours.
next_steps: 1) Eng to land hotfix PR to skip unnecessary compile for pinned models (owner: Priya Rao)
2) Run canary rollout with synthetic workloads against rw-llama-13b-v2 (owner: Diego Martinez)
3) After validation, schedule gradual rollout and monitor TTFB metrics and cache hit rates (owner: SRE)
4) CS to follow up with AcmeAnalytics in 24h and confirm restored performance
